title: Daddy Loves Your Toes
subtitle: a bedtime story for my little one

lines: Splish goes the water and splash goes the tub,
it's bubbles and duckies and rub-a-dub-dub.
And what's peeking up where the bubble-foam goes?
Ten slippery, wiggly, wet little toes!
I scrub every heel and I wash every sole,
you kick and you splash and you giggle and roll.
The duck says a quack, and the bubbles go pop,
and ten little tozies say, "Don't ever stop!"
Then out with a whoosh, in a towel warm and wide,
I dry every finger and toe, side to side.
A rub on your head and a boop on your nose,
and one extra kiss for those just-washed toes.
Then into pyjamas, all stars and moons bright,
the top goes on easy, the bottoms are tight.
I wiggle one leg in, and what do you know?
Pop! Out at the bottom, five toes say hello!
The other leg now, it goes tug, tug, and whee!
Five more little tozies come waving at me.
Then up for a cuddle, a squeeze and a spin,
and off to the big bed. It's time to climb in.
So climb onto Daddy, head down by my knees,
and feet by my face, if you please, if you please.
Here's one little piggy, and here's piggy two.
Those three in the middle? I don't know them. Do you?
Then five on the other, all wiggly and small,
ten little tozies, and I love them all.
You giggle and squirm when I tickle your feet,
you tell me they're stinky, I tell you they're sweet.
"Why do I need tozies? I've got such big feet!"
So Daddy can kiss them, and tickle, and eat!
And tozies hold steady so you don't fall down,
they carry you running all over the town.
They ran out to meet me when I came through the door,
they danced in the kitchen and stomped on the floor.
You laugh with your belly, you laugh with your nose,
you laugh all the way to the tips of your toes.
Now into your bed, and the lamp's turning low,
I'll sing you the song that you already know.
I sing to your nose and I sing to your hair,
and I sing to the tozies still wiggling there.
Sleep, little tozies, all soft in a row,
the moon's watching over, so gentle and slow.
Sleep, little feet, you've had such a big day.
You ran and you jumped and you danced and you played.
Your eyes getting heavy, your yawn big and slow,
I tuck in the blanket from top down to toe.
I'll keep them all warm and all safe through the night,
ten sleepy tozies, all tucked up tight.
From the top of your head to the tip of your nose,
but most of all, darling, Daddy loves your toes.
